Working document. One section per decision, ADR-style: context → options → decision → consequences. Decisions are revisable; flag any change with date and reason. The **Sign-off** column is the handover ownership track — every architectural decision needs a second signature before it's considered settled.

## Platform foundation

AIPLA sits on two open layers from the `sunholo-data` ecosystem, with the AIPLA-specific configuration on top:

- **[AI Protocol Platform](https://github.com/sunholo-data/ai-protocol-platform)** — open-source template (Apache 2.0) for the **application layer**: AG-UI streaming, A2UI declarative rendering, MCP tool integration, A2A agent discovery, ADK orchestration, multi-provider model routing, OpenTelemetry observability, `LOCAL_MODE` workshop path. Cloud-agnostic — runs on GCP, AWS, Azure, or on-premises. Used inside the Aitana assistant product among others.
- **Multivac** — Sunholo's wider AI platform, providing the **infrastructure layer**: managed model access (Vertex AI Gemini, Ollama hosting), Postgres + pgvector, Cloud Storage, identity, telemetry sinks. AIPLA's prototype runs on Multivac in an EU region; the [self-hosting](self-hosting.qmd) migration target is replacing Multivac with UCPH equivalents while keeping the template layer intact.

AIPLA-specific work is the configuration *on top* of both: physics skill packs, the [capability-floor router](evaluation.qmd) wiring, short-code session join (ADR-010), and EU-region constraints. See [ADR-001](#adr-001-cloud-provider-for-prototype-google-cloud-platform-eu) for the cloud/infrastructure decision and [ADR-011](#adr-011-strand-a-built-on-the-ai-protocol-platform) for the template adoption rationale and scope discipline.

## ADR-001 — Cloud provider for prototype: Google Cloud Platform (EU)

**Context.** JB's brief requires EU-hosted, GDPR-compliant infrastructure with no PII leakage to US providers where avoidable, holding up to UCPH data-protection review. Mid-July prototype deadline (~9 weeks) constrains us toward a managed stack.

**Options considered.**

- GCP EU regions (Vertex AI, Cloud Run, Firestore) — full stack from one vendor with EU residency
- AWS EU (Bedrock + Lambda) — comparable but Bedrock's Claude routing has US-control concerns
- Azure EU — workable but M less familiar
- Mistral La Plateforme + EU-hosted backend (Scaleway / Hetzner) — most EU-native but more pieces to assemble
- Pure self-host (UCPH server) — only viable if UCPH IT responds with a usable timeline

**Decision.** GCP EU for prototype, deployed via **Multivac** (Sunholo's AI platform — see [Platform foundation](#platform-foundation)). Vertex AI in europe-west3 (Frankfurt) or europe-west1 (Belgium) — pick one in ADR-002. Single-vendor EU-resident stack: cleanest DPA story for UCPH review.

**Consequences.**

- Multivac provides managed access to Vertex AI, Ollama hosting, Postgres, and Cloud Storage. AIPLA's infrastructure surface is Multivac's surface in the prototype.
- UCPH self-host migration becomes the dual track — see [Self-hosting](self-hosting.qmd). The application layer (template) is portable; the infrastructure layer (Multivac) is what gets swapped for UCPH equivalents.
- Cost is API-billed, not infrastructure-capex; tracked per-task via the capability-floor [evaluation](evaluation.qmd)
- M has Vertex AI familiarity (AILANG uses it) — reduces ramp time

## ADR-002 — Cloud region

**Context.** GCP offers europe-west1 (Belgium), europe-west3 (Frankfurt), europe-north1 (Finland), europe-west4 (Netherlands). For Danish school data, the relevant question is which EU region UCPH's data-protection team prefers and where Vertex AI Gemini is fully available.

**Pending:** confirm Vertex AI Gemini multimodal availability per region; confirm UCPH preference.

## ADR-003 — LLM provider mix (Claude · Gemini · Ollama)

**Context.** AIPLA needs strong text reasoning for problem-set hints and conceptual dialogue, strong multimodal for worksheet photos and diagram interpretation, EU data residency for student-facing use, and a credible path to self-hosted models for the [UCPH on-prem](self-hosting.qmd) migration target. No single provider gives the best answer across all three.

**Decision.** Four-tier model mix, routed **case-by-case per task class** via the [capability-floor eval](evaluation.qmd):

| Tier | Provider | Used for | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 — Cloud, cloud-agnostic | **Anthropic Claude** (Sonnet 4.6 / Haiku 4.5 / Opus 4.7) | Text reasoning — problem-set hints, conceptual dialogue, Socratic scaffolding, presentation critique | Strong reasoning; available via direct Anthropic API, AWS Bedrock, and GCP Vertex AI Model Garden — reduces single-cloud lock-in. |
| 2 — Cloud, EU-resident | **Google Gemini** (Vertex AI, EU region) | Multimodal — photos of free-body diagrams, Tracker screenshots, CSV / tabular reasoning | Best-in-class multimodal at price point; native EU residency. |
| 3 — Server-local | **Self-hosted Ollama** (UCPH GPU server, or M's 128GB Mac during prototyping) | Per-task-class adoption — only when the capability-floor eval shows an open-weight model meets the threshold for that class | Privacy-positive, zero API spend, no data crossing the institutional boundary. Adoption is **case-by-case**, not all-or-nothing. |
| 4 — On-device | **Apple Intelligence**, **Gemini Nano**, WebLLM / Transformers.js, or llama.cpp running on the student's device | Tasks the device can handle without help (light Q&A, summarisation, formatting), and offline scenarios | Gold standard for privacy — data literally never leaves the device. Also enables offline use, which is relevant for playground / lab / poor-WiFi settings mentioned in JB's brief. Constrained by device capability; included as a routing tier where it fits. |

Concrete model selection per task is driven by capability-floor eval results — see [Evaluation](evaluation.qmd).

**Consequences.**

- Routing layer (ADR-004) handles all four tiers behind one interface. The AI Protocol Platform template already supports multi-provider routing; the on-device tier requires a thin client-side adapter (most platforms expose simple JS APIs).
- **Cloud-agnosticism on the Claude path** is a strategic hedge: if AIPLA needs to move off GCP for any reason (UCPH preference, vendor change), Claude access doesn't have to change provider — only the auth endpoint.
- Cost mix: Haiku-class on cheap text tasks, Gemini Flash for cheap multimodal, Opus / Sonnet / Gemini Pro reserved for tasks the eval shows benefit from them. On-device tasks cost nothing.
- Migration trajectory: as the local-readiness fraction in the capability-floor eval rises, the server-local and on-device tiers grow; the cloud-provider share shrinks proportionally.
- **On-device tier viability is per-device**. A student on an iPad with Apple Intelligence has tier 4 available for certain tasks; a student on a basic Chromebook does not. The routing layer falls back gracefully (tier 4 → 3 → 2 → 1) when a higher-privacy tier isn't available for the given device or task.

## ADR-004 — Model abstraction / routing layer

**Context.** Brief implies and the 2026-05-15 conversation confirmed: provider should be a config swap, not a code change. Capability-floor eval determines which model is routed for which task class.

**Options to evaluate.**

- AILANG's existing OpenRouter + Ollama integration (Apache 2.0; pending JB discussion per ADR-009)
- LiteLLM (Python, broad provider support, mature)
- Vertex AI SDK direct + custom router
- Roll our own thin OpenAI-compatible adapter

**Pending.** Decision after ADR-009 resolved.

---

## ADR-005 — RAG store

**Context.** Teachers upload curriculum extracts, problem sets, lab guides. Bots retrieve at query time. Must be EU-resident.

**Options.**

- Vertex AI Vector Search (managed, EU-region, expensive at low volume)
- ChromaDB on Cloud Run + Cloud Storage (self-hosted, simple, cheap, fits our scale)
- pgvector on Cloud SQL Postgres (relational + vectors in one place)

**Lean.** pgvector — combines metadata, ACLs, and vectors in one place; cleanly migratable to UCPH-hosted Postgres later. Pending confirmation against teacher-upload volumes once JB clarifies scale.

## ADR-007 — Chat log storage + anonymisation

**Context.** Researcher access to chat logs is a core requirement. UCPH + Danish DPA consent forms (JB owns) define what we can store and for how long.

**Pending.** Anonymisation strategy depends on consent text. Working assumption: log retention with pseudonymous student IDs (per-session, per-class) and a separate identity map that researchers cannot access casually.

## ADR-008 — Multimodal input handling

**Context.** Photos of diagrams, screenshots of Tracker results, CSV/Excel exports. Gemini handles vision natively; tabular data via either direct upload or code execution.

**Pending.** Decide whether to do tabular data via Gemini's native handling or route through a code-execution sandbox (Cloud Run Jobs or similar). Code execution is needed anyway for Strand A's "geometry/arithmetic checks" requirement.

## ADR-009 — AILANG in production stack

**Context.** AILANG (Apache 2.0, M's project, ailang.sunholo.com) has the routing + Ollama integration that ADR-004 would otherwise require us to build. Using it as the production model-routing layer is a defensible architectural choice given M's authority but needs explicit disclosure to JB for visibility, not permission.

**Pending.** Conversation with JB. Possible outcomes:

- Use AILANG as the routing layer in production (cleanest technically)
- Use AILANG only for offline tooling (docparse, eval running) — production uses LiteLLM or similar
- Document AILANG as the prototype routing layer and migrate to a vendor-neutral library before handover

Until resolved, default to using AILANG for docparse and the eval runner (already in use, uncontroversial) and hold the production routing decision.

## ADR-010 — Student auth / identity

**Context.** Brief: "students/teachers don't need their own accounts or subscriptions." Project bills usage centrally. But chat logs must be researcher-retrievable per-session, per-class — so some session identity is needed.

**Pending.** Working assumption: short-code session join (teacher generates code, students join with code + first name or pseudonym). No persistent accounts. Per-class, per-session identity is enough for the research data, and minimises PII surface.

## ADR-011 — Strand A built on the AI Protocol Platform

**Context.** Building Strand A's pedagogical bot infrastructure from scratch within the four-month contract is feasible but tight: GDPR-grade auth, multi-provider model routing, log capture with anonymisation, multimodal upload handling, teacher-facing skill configuration, and the supporting telemetry are each multi-week tracks. The [AI Protocol Platform](https://github.com/sunholo-data/ai-protocol-platform) (Apache 2.0, public repo on the `sunholo-data` org) is an open-source template that already solves most of these. It is cloud-agnostic (GCP, AWS, Azure, on-prem) and designed by M to serve a class of projects including AIPLA — already used inside Sunholo's wider Multivac AI platform offering and in the Aitana assistant product.

**What the template provides off the shelf:**

- **Protocols** — AG-UI streaming, A2UI declarative rendering, MCP tool integration, A2A agent discovery
- **Orchestration** — Google ADK with sessions, memory, artifacts, evaluation
- **Multi-provider model routing** — Gemini, Claude, OpenAI through one interface
- **Observability** — OpenTelemetry → Cloud Trace + Cloud Logging + BigQuery, all internal-trust-boundary
- **`LOCAL_MODE`** — clone-to-working-chat-UI in under 30 minutes, no cloud credentials required. Critical for postdoc-2 onboarding and for any teacher dialogue session where we want a portable demo.
- **Skills wizard** — non-developer skill creation, matching the brief's "teacher bot configuration" requirement
- **LaTeX rendering** — already supported via the ailang-parse integration (relevant for physics formulae output)

**Options considered.**

- Build Strand A bot infrastructure from scratch in Python/FastAPI on Cloud Run (originally implied by ADR-001)
- Adopt LangChain or a similar open-source framework as the base
- Adopt the AI Protocol Platform template as the foundation and add AIPLA-specific configuration on top

**Decision.** Adopt the AI Protocol Platform template. AIPLA work is the configuration, skill packs, EU-region pinning, short-code session join, and self-host migration path on top of an already-mature template.

**Scope discipline.** The template has more surface area than AIPLA needs in four months. The risk is that *because* features exist, we feel obliged to use them. Explicit opt-in list for AIPLA v1:

| Feature | AIPLA v1 | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Web frontend + AG-UI streaming | ✅ Use | Core teacher/student UI |
| Skills wizard + skill configuration | ✅ Use | Matches brief requirement directly |
| Multi-provider model routing | ✅ Use | Wired to capability-floor eval |
| LOCAL_MODE | ✅ Use | Postdoc-2 onboarding, portable demos |
| Anonymised chat-log capture | ✅ Use | Core research data requirement |
| LaTeX rendering | ✅ Use | Physics formula output |
| A2UI declarative components | ✅ Use sparingly | For structured outputs (problem-set hints, etc.) |
| MCP tool integration | ✅ Use selectively | Code execution sandbox for geometry/arithmetic |
| MCP Apps (sandboxed iframes) | 🟡 Strand B target | Holds the simulation/game artefacts cleanly |
| A2A agent discovery | ❌ Skip v1 | Useful long-term, not required for the pilot |
| Telegram / Email / WhatsApp channels | ❌ Skip v1 | Available; not needed for STX teacher pilot |
| Vertex AI Search | ❌ Skip v1 | pgvector covers AIPLA's RAG needs per ADR-005 |
| Real-time collaboration features | ❌ Skip v1 | Out of brief scope |

**Disclosure (handover & conflict of interest).** The AI Protocol Platform is M's own work. This is parallel to the AILANG disclosure in [ADR-009](#adr-009-ailang-in-production-stack) and needs the same explicit visibility with JB. Three mitigating points:

- The template is Apache 2.0 licensed and the repo is public; AIPLA's open-source-at-end-of-project goal is fully compatible
- The template is multi-purpose — designed for a class of projects, not AIPLA-specific. AILANG itself is not required to use the template (it's used inside the platform for LaTeX parsing and capability benchmarks, but the template supports plain Python stacks)
- M's architectural authority on AIPLA (per JB's brief) covers this kind of choice, but the choice should be *named* rather than implicit

**Consequences.**

- **Build-time saving.** What would otherwise be ~6 of the 9 Strand A build weeks is absorbed by the template. Frees time for physics-specific extensions, the capability-floor eval, and the teacher pilot.
- **UCPH self-host implications.** A few template defaults (Firestore for some session data, Firebase Auth for non-LOCAL_MODE) don't have direct UCPH-on-prem equivalents. The [self-hosting](self-hosting.qmd) page needs to expand to cover these. UCPH IT conversation needs to be informed by the template's actual dependencies, not a generic GCP stack.
- **Handover surface.** P2 and successors need to understand the template's structure to maintain AIPLA. The template's own documentation and the `LOCAL_MODE` workshop story help here — successors can spin up the platform locally without cloud credentials and learn it without risk.
- **Update cadence.** The template evolves on its own roadmap (driven by Multivac and Aitana usage). AIPLA will need to track upstream changes. Acceptable risk during the contract (M is the maintainer); needs an explicit version-pinning + upstream-tracking strategy in the handover package.

## ADR-012 — Document parsing via AILANG Parse

**Context.** AIPLA bots ingest teacher and student documents: lesson plans (DOCX), worksheets, sensor exports (CSV/XLSX), email threads (EML), presentation slides (PPTX), lab reports (PDF), photos of hand-drawn diagrams (PNG/JPG). The naive approach — pass every upload to a multimodal LLM for extraction — is wasteful in tokens, slow, and substantially weaker on the GDPR/privacy axis than is necessary.

**What [AILANG Parse](https://github.com/sunholo-data/ailang-parse) (Apache 2.0) provides.**

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    Upload[Uploaded document]
    Parse{AILANG Parse}
    Det["Deterministic XML parse<br/>13 formats · zero LLM tokens<br/>DOCX · PPTX · XLSX · ODT · ODP · ODS<br/>HTML · MD · CSV · EPUB · EML · MBOX · TEX"]
    AI["AI multimodal extraction<br/>2 formats · routed via model router<br/>PDF · images"]
    Out["Structured blocks<br/>+ markdown"]

    Upload --> Parse
    Parse --> Det
    Parse --> AI
    Det --> Out
    AI --> Out

    style Det fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2d7d3a
    style AI fill:#fce7e8,stroke:#901a1e
    style Parse fill:#f5f5f5,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px
```

The deterministic path is the load-bearing one for privacy: a Word document or Excel sheet uploaded by a teacher is parsed by reading the file's XML directly. **The content never reaches an LLM.** That covers the majority of formats used in Danish stx physics teaching: lesson materials, problem sets, lab data exports, email correspondence.

The AI path is only invoked for genuinely image-shaped content — scanned PDFs, photos of hand-drawn diagrams. Those go through the same [capability-floor eval](evaluation.qmd)–driven model router as chat tasks, with the same option to route to a local Ollama model when on-prem deployment matures.

**Decision.** Document upload pipeline routes through AILANG Parse first. Office and structured formats take the deterministic path. PDF and image extraction routes through the template's model router; the capability-floor eval determines which model handles which kind of PDF/image task.

**Why this is a strong GDPR move.**

| Format | What gets parsed | Where the content goes |
|---|---|---|
| DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, ODT, ODP, ODS | Lesson plans, slides, worksheets, exports | Local parsing — no external call |
| CSV, EML, MBOX, HTML, MD, TEX, EPUB | Tabular data, email, structured text | Local parsing — no external call |
| PDF, JPG, PNG | Scans, hand-drawn diagrams, screenshots | Multimodal LLM via model router (EU region; local Ollama future) |

For a UCPH data-protection review, "13 of 15 supported formats never leave the trust boundary" is a stronger story than any single-vendor multimodal approach.

**Disclosure.** AILANG Parse is part of the AILANG ecosystem ([ADR-009](#adr-009-ailang-in-production-stack)) — same disclosure considerations apply. It is published as a standalone Apache 2.0 library with Python, JavaScript, and Go SDKs and is used by projects beyond AIPLA. The AI Protocol Platform template integrates it natively.

**Consequences.**

- **Cost.** Substantially fewer LLM tokens consumed on document ingest. The capability-floor eval will quantify by how much.
- **Latency.** Deterministic XML parsing is sub-second; multimodal extraction is multi-second. Most uploads land instantly.
- **UCPH self-host friendliness.** AILANG Parse runs anywhere — CLI binary, Python SDK, or local service. No cloud dependency. Integrates cleanly with the [self-hosting](self-hosting.qmd) migration path.
- **Calibration tracking.** Extraction quality is part of the capability-floor benchmark: for PDF/image tasks (T5 — worksheet OCR, T6 — tabular data interpretation), comparing AILANG-Parse-via-Gemini, AILANG-Parse-via-local-Ollama, and the underlying alternatives is exactly what the eval is designed for.
